svg.text: A type-0 enemy record: 25 bytes at $ED49 + 25n (the other drivers use the same layout with a few extra bytes)

g.text: bit 0 on the field, 1 dying, 2 in a bubble, 3 gone, 4 killed by a bubble pop, 5 entrance done, 6 released, 7 angry
position, from the object slot; also copied to the shared records at $ED21 for the MCU and the sub CPU
handed out by the slot allocator at round start
the walk cycle, or the tumble while dying
0 idle, 1 walking right, 2 falling, 3 walking left, 4 jumping (from a right walk), 5 jumping (from a left walk)
1 right, 3 left: which way to face and which walk state to land in
0-6: selects the 4-byte shared record at $ED21 and the 8-byte MCU result at $FC27
speed list index, speed list, step
the same lists at $11CE as the players and bubbles: the record's [8] normally, +6 when angry, capped at 40
bit 1 moved this frame, bit 5 fell, bit 6 the angry speed applied, bit 7 the hurry-up speed; while dying: the death state
set when the player is within 32 lines vertically; while dead: which player collected the fruit
the movement script (a jump or a turn); during the entrance: the step timer and the target line
frames spent against a wall; at 60 the enemy jumps out of the corner
counts down to the next chase-or-jump decision; while dead: the fruit index
120 at start; while dead: the 60-frame pauses of the fruit
0 normally; 3 marks a variant that never chases; the death tumble reads it as its frame base
bit 0 a jump script is running, bit 1 the next decision is a jump (toggles), bit 2 landed, bit 7 the jump script is armed
The shared record at $ED21 + 4n is [flags, x, y, result]: flags bit 0 = on the field for the sub CPU and the MCU, $80 = caught in a bubble,
$40 = dead and falling, $20 = escaped angry, $10 = caught by an item, 8 = lying as fruit; the result byte carries the sub CPU's touch report,
the chain place that chooses the fruit, or which player picked it up (bit 7 = player 2).
The type-2 record is 35 bytes (a second slot and sprite for the rock in hand); type 3 has 27 (the shot budget); the bouncers keep their scripts in the same bytes.
